text: The $\text{Organism}$ $\text{Responsible}$ for the $\text{Nitrogen}$ $\text{Fixation}$ in the $\text{Root}$ $\text{Nodules}$ of $\text{Leguminous}$ $\text{Plants}$ is:
image: [Diagram of a leguminous plant root with nodules]
explanation: $\text{Rhizobium}$ is a genus of $\text{Soil}$ $\text{Bacteria}$ that forms a $\text{Symbiotic}$ relationship with $\text{Legumes}$, residing in the root nodules where they convert atmospheric $\text{Nitrogen}$ ($	ext{N}_2$) into $\text{Ammonia}$ ($	ext{NH}_3$). The processes carried out by $\text{Nitrobacter}$ and $\text{Nitrosomonas}$ are part of $\text{Nitrification}$, not fixation.

text: Which of the following is $\text{NOT}$ a $\text{Sense}$ $\text{Organ}$ in $\text{Mammals}$?
explanation: The $\text{Cochlea}$ is a $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Inner}$ $\text{Ear}$ responsible for $\text{Hearing}$, while the $\text{Ear}$ as a whole is the sense organ. The $\text{Skin}$ (touch/temperature), $\text{Tongue}$ (taste), and $\text{Nose}$ (smell) are recognized as sense organs.

text: The $\text{Hormone}$ that $\text{Stimulates}$ the $\text{Conversion}$ of $\text{Glycogen}$ to $\text{Glucose}$ in the $\text{Liver}$ is:
image: [Diagram illustrating the effect of Glucagon and Insulin on blood sugar]
explanation: $\text{Glucagon}$, secreted by the $\text{Pancreas}$, acts on the $\text{Liver}$ to $\text{Increase}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Sugar}$ levels by promoting $\text{Glycogenolysis}$ (breaking down glycogen to glucose).

text: The $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Material}$ in a $\text{Bacterium}$ is found in the:
image: [Diagram of a bacterial cell showing the nucleoid region]
explanation: Bacteria are $\text{Prokaryotic}$ organisms and $\text{Lack}$ a $\text{True}$ $\text{Nucleus}$. Their $\text{Circular}$ $\text{DNA}$ is concentrated in a region of the $\text{Cytoplasm}$ called the $\text{Nucleoid}$.

text: The $\text{Waste}$ $\text{Product}$ of $\text{Photosynthesis}$ that is $\text{Essential}$ for $\text{Respiration}$ is:
image: [Chemical equation for photosynthesis]
explanation: $\text{Oxygen}$ ($	ext{O}_2$) is $\text{Released}$ into the $\text{Atmosphere}$ as a $\text{Byproduct}$ of the $\text{Light}$-$\text{Dependent}$ $\text{Reactions}$ of $\text{Photosynthesis}$ and is required for $\text{Aerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ in most organisms.

text: Which of these $\text{Cells}$ $\text{Lacks}$ a $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$?
image: [Diagram showing the difference between plant and animal cells]
explanation: $\text{Animal}$ $\text{Cells}$ are $\text{Surrounded}$ only by a $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$. $\text{Fungi}$ (chitin), $\text{Bacteria}$ (peptidoglycan), and $\text{Plants}$ (cellulose) all possess a $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$.

text: The $\text{Structure}$ responsible for $\text{Exchange}$ of $\text{Gases}$ in $\text{Flowering}$ $\text{Plants}$' $\text{Stems}$ is the:
image: [Microscopic view of Lenticels on a woody stem]
explanation: In $\text{Woody}$ $\text{Stems}$ and $\text{Roots}$, $\text{Gas}$ $\text{Exchange}$ occurs through $\text{Lenticels}$, which are $\text{Porous}$ $\text{Areas}$ in the $\text{Bark}$. $\text{Stomata}$ are found mostly on $\text{Leaves}$.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Ear}$ that $\text{Balances}$ $\text{Pressure}$ between the $\text{Middle}$ $\text{Ear}$ and the $\text{Outside}$ $\text{Atmosphere}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human ear highlighting the Eustachian Tube]
explanation: The $\text{Eustachian}$ $\text{Tube}$ (or $\text{Auditory}$ $\text{Tube}$) $\text{Connects}$ the $\text{Middle}$ $\text{Ear}$ to the $\text{Naso}$-$\text{Pharynx}$, allowing air pressure on both sides of the $\text{Eardrum}$ (Tympanic membrane) to equalize.

text: An $\text{Organism}$ that $\text{Feeds}$ on $\text{Dead}$ $\text{Organic}$ $\text{Matter}$ is termed a:
image: [Diagram showing examples of different feeding types, including a scavenger]
explanation: $\text{Saprophytes}$ (like $\text{Fungi}$ and $\text{Bacteria}$) are $\text{Heterotrophs}$ that $\text{Digest}$ and $\text{Absorb}$ nutrients from $\text{Dead}$ and $\text{Decaying}$ $\text{Matter}$. $\text{Scavengers}$ are large animals that eat dead animals.

text: A $\text{Population}$ that is $\text{Increasing}$ $\text{Rapidly}$ is typically characterized by a large proportion of:
image: [Age pyramid showing a rapidly growing population structure (wide base)]
explanation: In a $\text{Rapidly}$ $\text{Growing}$ $\text{Population}$, the base of the $\text{Age}$ $\text{Pyramid}$ (the $\text{Young}$, pre-reproductive group) is the $\text{Widest}$, indicating high birth rates and potential for future growth.

text: The $\text{Condition}$ of $\text{Lack}$ of $\text{Blood}$ due to a $\text{Deficiency}$ of $\text{Iron}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Anaemia}$ is a condition characterized by a $\text{Reduced}$ $\text{Number}$ of $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ or $\text{Haemoglobin}$. $\text{Iron}$ $\text{Deficiency}$ is the $\text{Most}$ $\text{Common}$ $\text{Cause}$ as $\text{Iron}$ is needed to $\text{Synthesize}$ $\text{Haemoglobin}$.

text: Which of these features $\text{Best}$ distinguishes a $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cell}$ from an $\text{Animal}$ $\text{Cell}$?
image: [Venn diagram or table comparing plant and animal cell organelles]
explanation: While both cell types share a $\text{Nucleus}$, $\text{Cytoplasm}$, and $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$, only $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cells}$ typically possess a $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$ (for structure) and $\text{Chloroplasts}$ (for $\text{Photosynthesis}$).

text: The $\text{Most}$ $\text{Effective}$ way of $\text{Controlling}$ the $\text{Spread}$ of $\text{Typhoid}$ $\text{Fever}$ is through:
explanation: $\text{Typhoid}$ is a $\text{Water}$-borne $\text{Disease}$ caused by $\text{Salmonella}$ $\text{Typhi}$. Ensuring a clean, $\text{Uncontaminated}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Supply}$ is the $\text{Most}$ $\text{Crucial}$ $\text{Measure}$ for control.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Inheritance}$ of $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Groups}$ in humans is an example of:
image: [Punnett square showing inheritance patterns for ABO blood groups]
explanation: Human $\text{ABO}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Groups}$ are determined by $\text{Three}$ $\text{Alleles}$ ($	ext{I}^{\text{A}}, \text{I}^{\text{B}}, \text{i}$), making it an example of $\text{Multiple}$ $\text{Alleles}$. It also demonstrates $\text{Co}$-$\text{Dominance}$ ($	ext{AB}$ blood group).

text: Which of the following is an $\text{Arachnid}$?
explanation: $\text{Arachnids}$ (Spiders, $\text{Scorpions}$, $\text{Ticks}$) are $\text{Arthropods}$ characterized by having $\text{Four}$ $\text{Pairs}$ of $\text{Legs}$ (8 legs) and $\text{Two}$ $\text{Body}$ $\text{Parts}$ (Cephalothorax and Abdomen). $\text{Cockroaches}$ (Insects) have 6 legs.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Forebrain}$ that controls $\text{Body}$ $\text{Temperature}$ and $\text{Osmoregulation}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human brain highlighting the Hypothalamus]
explanation: The $\text{Hypothalamus}$ is a $\text{Major}$ $\text{Centre}$ for $\text{Homeostasis}$ and is crucial for regulating body $\text{Temperature}$, $\text{Thirst}$, $\text{Hunger}$, and $\text{Water}$ $\text{Balance}$ ($	ext{Osmoregulation}$).

text: The $\text{Process}$ by which $\text{Digested}$ $\text{Food}$ is $\text{Absorbed}$ into the $\text{Bloodstream}$ in the $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$ is called:
image: [Diagram of a villus showing absorption of nutrients]
explanation: $\text{Absorption}$ is the $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Nutrients}$ from the $\text{Digestive}$ $\text{Tract}$ into the $\text{Circulatory}$ $\text{System}$. $\text{Assimilation}$ is the $\text{Use}$ of these absorbed nutrients by the body cells.

text: Which of these is $\text{NOT}$ a $\text{Product}$ of $\text{Kidney}$ $\text{Excretion}$ in $\text{Mammals}$?
explanation: $\text{Bile}$ $\text{Pigments}$ ($	ext{Bilirubin}$, $	ext{Biliverdin}$) are $\text{Breakdown}$ $\text{Products}$ of $\text{Haemoglobin}$ and are $\text{Excreted}$ by the $\text{Liver}$ into the $\text{Faeces}$, $\text{Not}$ primarily by the $\text{Kidneys}$ in $\text{Urine}$.

text: The $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Nucleolus}$ is primarily for the $\text{Synthesis}$ of:
image: [Diagram of the nucleus showing the nucleolus]
explanation: The $\text{Nucleolus}$ is the $\text{Site}$ within the $\text{Nucleus}$ where $\text{Ribosomal}$ $\text{RNA}$ ($	ext{rRNA}$) is $\text{Synthesized}$ and $\text{Assembled}$ with $\text{Proteins}$ to $\text{Form}$ $\text{Ribosomes}$.

text: The $\text{Adaptation}$ that allows $\text{Terrestrial}$ $\text{Insects}$ to $\text{Conserve}$ $\text{Water}$ is the excretion of $\text{Nitrogenous}$ $\text{Waste}$ as:
explanation: $\text{Uric}$ $\text{Acid}$ is the $\text{Least}$ $\text{Toxic}$ and $\text{Least}$ $\text{Water}$-$	ext{Soluble}$ of the nitrogenous wastes. Excreting it as a $\text{Semi}$-$\text{Solid}$ $\text{Paste}$ (via $\text{Malpighian}$ $\text{Tubules}$) allows insects to $\text{Minimize}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Loss}$.

text: A $\text{Feature}$ that $\text{Unites}$ $\text{Reptiles}$, $\text{Birds}$, and $\text{Mammals}$ is the presence of:
image: [Diagram of an amniotic egg]
explanation: $\text{Reptiles}$, $\text{Birds}$, and $\text{Mammals}$ (whose embryos develop in a $\text{Fluid}$-filled $\text{Amniotic}$ $\text{Sac}$) are collectively called $\text{Amniotes}$. This is a key adaptation for $\text{Life}$ on $\text{Land}$.

text: The $\text{Force}$ that causes $\text{Water}$ to $\text{Move}$ from the $\text{Roots}$ to the $\text{Leaves}$ in $\text{Tall}$ $\text{Trees}$ is primarily:
image: [Diagram illustrating the cohesive-tension theory of water transport in xylem]
explanation: $\text{Transpiration}$ $\text{Pull}$ (Cohesion-Tension $\text{Mechanism}$) is the $\text{Major}$ $\text{Force}$ responsible for $\text{Lifting}$ $\text{Water}$ in the $\text{Xylem}$ against $\text{Gravity}$. It is created by the $\text{Evaporation}$ of water from the leaves.

text: The $\text{Type}$ of $\text{Variation}$ that gives rise to a $\text{Smooth}$ $\text{Bell}$-$\text{Shaped}$ $\text{Curve}$ when plotted is:
image: [Graph showing a normal distribution curve for continuous variation]
explanation: $\text{Continuous}$ $\text{Variation}$ involves traits (like $\text{Height}$, $\text{Weight}$) that $\text{Vary}$ $\text{Gradually}$ and are typically controlled by $\text{Many}$ $\text{Genes}$. When plotted, they follow a $\text{Normal}$ $\text{Distribution}$ ($	ext{Bell}$ $\text{Curve}$).

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Flower}$ that $\text{Develops}$ into the $\text{Fruit}$ after $\text{Fertilization}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a flower showing the ovary and its development into fruit]
explanation: After $\text{Fertilization}$, the $\text{Ovules}$ develop into $\text{Seeds}$, and the $\text{Ovary}$ wall usually $\text{Develops}$ and $\text{Matures}$ into the $\text{Fruit}$ wall ($	ext{Pericarp}$).

text: Which of the following is $\text{TRUE}$ of the $\text{Movement}$ of the $\text{Cytoplasm}$ in $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cells}$?
explanation: $\text{Cyclosis}$ is the $\text{Streaming}$ or $\text{Circulation}$ of the $\text{Cytoplasm}$ within a $\text{Cell}$. This movement $\text{Facilitates}$ the $\text{Distribution}$ of $\text{Nutrients}$ and $\text{Organelles}$.

text: The $\text{Causative}$ $\text{Organism}$ of $\text{Sleeping}$ $\text{Sickness}$ is a $\text{Protozoan}$ transmitted by the:
explanation: The $\text{Protozoan}$ $\text{Trypanosoma}$ $\text{brucei}$ causes $\text{Sleeping}$ $\text{Sickness}$ (African $\text{Trypanosomiasis}$), which is transmitted by the bite of the $\text{Tsetse}$ $\text{Fly}$ ($	ext{Genus}$ $\text{Glossina}$). The $\text{Black}$ $\text{Fly}$ transmits $\text{River}$ $\text{Blindness}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Growth}$ in $\text{Plants}$ that is $\text{Irreversible}$ and $\text{Permanent}$ is called:
explanation: In biology, true $\text{Growth}$ involves an $\text{Irreversible}$ $\text{Increase}$ in $\text{Size}$ or $\text{Mass}$ (due to cell $\text{Division}$ and $\text{Enlargement}$ ($	ext{Elongation}$)). $\text{Plasmolysis}$ is a reversible shrinkage.

text: The $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Vessel}$ that $\text{Carries}$ $\text{Deoxygenated}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Away}$ from the $\text{Heart}$ to the $\text{Lungs}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human heart showing pulmonary circulation]
explanation: The $\text{Pulmonary}$ $\text{Artery}$ is the $\text{Only}$ $\text{Artery}$ that carries $\text{Deoxygenated}$ $\text{Blood}$. It takes the blood from the $\text{Right}$ $\text{Ventricle}$ of the heart to the $\text{Lungs}$ for oxygenation.

text: The $\text{Enzyme}$ that $\text{Digests}$ $\text{Starch}$ into $\text{Maltose}$ is:
image: [Diagram illustrating the action of Amylase]
explanation: $\text{Amylase}$ (found in saliva and pancreatic juice) is the enzyme responsible for $\text{Breaking}$ $\text{Down}$ $\text{Starch}$ (a $\text{Polysaccharide}$) into the $\text{Disaccharide}$ $\text{Maltose}$.

text: A $\text{Pollen}$ $\text{Grain}$ lands on the $\text{Stigma}$ of a flower of the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Species}$. This is specifically known as:
image: [Diagram showing self-pollination vs. cross-pollination]
explanation: $\text{Pollination}$ is the $\text{Transfer}$ of $\text{Pollen}$ from the $\text{Anther}$ to the $\text{Stigma}$. When this $\text{Transfer}$ occurs within the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Flower}$ or between flowers of the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Plant}$, it is called $\text{Self}$ $\text{Pollination}$ or $\text{Autogamy}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Development}$ from a $\text{Zygote}$ to an $\text{Embryo}$ in humans is called:
image: [Diagram showing stages of human embryonic development from fertilization to implantation]
explanation: $\text{Embryogenesis}$ encompasses the stages of development from the $\text{Fertilized}$ $\text{Egg}$ ($	ext{Zygote}$) through $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Division}$ ($	ext{Cleavage}$) and $\text{Formation}$ of $\text{Germ}$ $\text{Layers}$ ($	ext{Gastrulation}$) to the $\text{Embryo}$.

text: The $\text{Loss}$ of $\text{Water}$ in the form of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Vapour}$ from the $\text{Aerial}$ $\text{Parts}$ of a $\text{Plant}$ is:
image: [Diagram illustrating transpiration through stomata]
explanation: $\text{Transpiration}$ is the $\text{Evaporation}$ of $\text{Water}$ from $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Leaves}$ and $\text{Stems}$. $\text{Guttation}$ is the $\text{Loss}$ of $\text{Liquid}$ $\text{Water}$ droplets from leaves.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Eye}$ that $\text{Contains}$ $\text{Light}$-$\text{Sensitive}$ $\text{Cells}$ ($	ext{Rods}$ and $\text{Cones}$) is the:
image: [Diagram of the human eye showing the Retina]
explanation: The $\text{Retina}$ is the $\text{Innermost}$ $\text{Layer}$ at the $\text{Back}$ of the $\text{Eye}$ that $\text{Contains}$ $\text{Photoreceptor}$ $\text{Cells}$ ($	ext{Rods}$ and $\text{Cones}$), which convert light into nerve impulses.

text: A $\text{Relationship}$ where $\text{One}$ $\text{Organism}$ $\text{Benefits}$ and the $\text{Other}$ is $\text{Neither}$ $\text{Helped}$ $\text{Nor}$ $\text{Harmed}$ is called:
image: [Diagram illustrating a commensal relationship (e.g., barnacles on a whale)]
explanation: In $\text{Commensalism}$, one organism ($	ext{The}$ $\text{Commensal}$) $\text{Benefits}$ from the relationship, while the other organism ($	ext{The}$ $\text{Host}$) is $\text{Unaffected}$.

text: The $\text{Final}$ $\text{Acceptor}$ of $\text{Electrons}$ in the $\text{Electron}$ $\text{Transport}$ $\text{Chain}$ of $\text{Aerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ is:
image: [Diagram of the Electron Transport Chain in the mitochondrion]
explanation: In $\text{Aerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$, $\text{Oxygen}$ acts as the $\text{Terminal}$ $\text{Electron}$ $\text{Acceptor}$ at the $\text{End}$ of the $\text{Electron}$ $\text{Transport}$ $\text{Chain}$, forming $\text{Water}$ ($	ext{H}_2\text{O}$).

text: Which of the following $\text{Organisms}$ belongs to the $\text{Phylum}$ $\text{Arthropoda}$?
image: [Diagram comparing different arthropod classes (Insecta, Crustacea, Arachnida)]
explanation: $\text{Arthropoda}$ is the $\text{Largest}$ $\text{Phylum}$ in the animal kingdom, characterized by $\text{Jointed}$ $\text{Legs}$ and a $\text{Chitinous}$ $\text{Exoskeleton}$. $\text{Butterflies}$ are $\text{Insects}$, which belong to the $\text{Arthropoda}$ phylum. $\text{Earthworm}$ is an $\text{Annelid}$, $\text{Snail}$ is a $\text{Mollusc}$.

text: The $\text{Main}$ $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Chloroplasts}$ in a plant cell is:
image: [Diagram of a chloroplast showing thylakoids and stroma]
explanation: $\text{Chloroplasts}$ contain the pigment $\text{Chlorophyll}$ and are the $\text{Sites}$ of $\text{Photosynthesis}$, the process that converts light energy into chemical energy ($	ext{Glucose}$).

text: If a plant with $\text{Red}$ $\text{Flowers}$ ($	ext{RR}$) is crossed with a plant with $\text{White}$ $\text{Flowers}$ ($	ext{rr}$) and the $\text{F}_1$ generation produces $\text{Pink}$ $\text{Flowers}$ ($	ext{Rr}$), this indicates:
image: [Diagram illustrating incomplete dominance (red x white -> pink)]
explanation: $\text{Incomplete}$ $\text{Dominance}$ is a form of inheritance in which $\text{Neither}$ $\text{Allele}$ is $\text{Completely}$ $\text{Dominant}$, resulting in a $\text{Phenotype}$ that is a $\text{Mixture}$ or $\text{Intermediate}$ of the two parental phenotypes ($	ext{Pink}$ in this case).

text: The $\text{Deficiency}$ of $\text{Vitamin}$ $\text{C}$ in humans results in a disease known as:
explanation: $\text{Scurvy}$ is caused by $\text{Chronic}$ $\text{Lack}$ of $\text{Vitamin}$ $\text{C}$ ($	ext{Ascorbic}$ $\text{Acid}$), which is $\text{Essential}$ for the $\text{Synthesis}$ of $\text{Collagen}$ and $\text{Connective}$ $\text{Tissue}$. $\text{Rickets}$ is Vitamin $\text{D}$ deficiency, and $\text{Beriberi}$ is Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ deficiency.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Widespread}$ $\text{Introduction}$ of $\text{New}$ $\text{Plant}$ and $\text{Animal}$ $\text{Species}$ into an $\text{Ecosystem}$ is most likely to lead to:
image: [Image illustrating invasive species displacing native species]
explanation: The $\text{Introduction}$ of $\text{Exotic}$ or $\text{Invasive}$ $\text{Species}$ often leads to $\text{Competition}$, $\text{Predation}$, and $\text{Disease}$, resulting in the $\text{Decline}$ or $\text{Extinction}$ of $\text{Native}$ $\text{Species}$ and a $\text{Reduction}$ in local $\text{Biodiversity}$.
